svg.text: hash_engine: SHA3-256 over host flash or processor written data
Flash fetch: the same command/response channel the eSPI flash reads use
The engine issues one command for the whole range. Chunking, and winning the shared SPI engine, happen on the far side.
Abandoning a read. The transaction manager cannot be called off, so an abort or restart goes through DRAIN and discards
exactly the bytes still owed. busy stays set until that finishes, which is why software must poll it before reusing the engine.
When the software FIFO is flushed. At the *end* of a run, not the start. Flushing at the start races with a processor that
polls wfifo_full, sees it clear, and then writes: the write lands inside the flush window and disappears. Flushing at the end
means a run always begins with a FIFO already known clean.
